input_candidates.spec:
Design a synthesizable ASIC digital IP block named active_aero_ctrl_top that implements safety-supervised command handling around an external DoMINO automotive aerodynamics surrogate. The physics model itself is not part of RTL and shall be treated as an off-chip or off-block service accessed via a valid/ready style transaction interface. The top-level block shall include: (1) a configuration input path for vehicle_geometry metadata, including geometry_source, geometry_format, and geometry_id; (2) a runtime input path for flow_conditions containing stream_velocity_mps and a flow_valid qualifier; (3) a model request output channel carrying req_valid, req_id, vehicle_geometry, and flow_conditions to the external surrogate; (4) a model response input channel carrying rsp_valid, rsp_id, drag_force, lift_force, surface_pressure, and flow_field metadata; (5) an actuator output channel carrying actuator_cmd and actuator_valid; and (6) a status channel carrying fallback_active, stale_reject, timeout_fault, cmd_clamped, status_code, and fault_code.

The design shall be fully synchronous to clk and reset_n. reset_n shall be active-low and shall initialize all state elements, request sequence counters, pending request flags, timeout counters, safety flags, actuator registers, and telemetry registers to the safe state. The safe state shall assert fallback_active, deassert actuator_valid, and drive actuator_cmd to a configured safe default value. The safe default value shall be registered and synthesizable as a constant or parameter.

The request manager shall capture a new flow_conditions sample only when flow_valid is asserted and the sample lies within the allowed operating envelope. The valid operating envelope shall be parameterized but constrained by the supplied requirement to stream_velocity_mps between 20 and 55 inclusive. If the flow velocity is outside this range, the supervisor shall inhibit model request issuance and force safe fallback for the current cycle and subsequent cycles until a valid sample is accepted. The request manager shall generate a monotonically incrementing req_id for each new request transaction. A request shall be marked pending after req_valid is asserted and shall remain pending until a matching response is accepted or a timeout occurs.

The response monitor shall accept a response only when rsp_valid is asserted, rsp_id matches the outstanding req_id, and the response integrity checks pass. Integrity checks shall include sequence match, non-zero/valid payload qualifiers where available, and freshness timing. If rsp_id does not match the outstanding req_id, the response shall be discarded and stale_reject shall be asserted for that transaction. If the response is received after the programmable timeout count expires, timeout_fault shall be asserted and the response shall be ignored. The timeout counter shall be synthesized as a down counter or age counter driven by clock cycles while a request is pending. The timeout value shall be a parameter with a reset default suitable for ASIC integration.

The command synthesis unit shall be a deterministic digital control block that maps the validated surrogate outputs into an actuator command candidate. The RTL shall not implement the surrogate physics computation; instead it shall accept validated model outputs and produce a candidate command based on a configurable policy table, lookup, arithmetic scaling, or fixed-point combinational logic. The command path shall support a single registered output update per accepted response. The command candidate shall then pass through a clamp and optional rate-limiter stage. The clamp stage shall enforce a minimum and maximum actuator command bound using compare-and-select logic. If the candidate exceeds bounds, cmd_clamped shall be asserted and the output shall be driven to the nearest boundary. If rate limiting is enabled, the output shall not change faster than a parameterized delta per update, implemented using registered previous output and saturating add/sub logic.

The safety supervisor shall arbitrate between normal command flow and fallback. If any of the following conditions are true, the supervisor shall suppress normal actuator updates and select safe fallback: stale response detected, timeout detected, response invalid, response not aligned with outstanding request, flow velocity out of envelope, or reset asserted. When fallback is active, actuator_valid shall be low and actuator_cmd shall be equal to the safe default value or a safe-state register value. The supervisor shall retain fallback_active until a valid request-response cycle is completed and all safety conditions clear. Recovery from fallback shall be synchronous and deterministic; no asynchronous release behavior is allowed.

The design shall expose traceability registers for req_id, rsp_id, status_code, and fault_code. status_code shall encode at least: idle, request_pending, response_accepted, fallback_active, and faulted. fault_code shall encode at least: none, stale_response, timeout, envelope_violation, integrity_error, and clamp_event. The encoding shall be parameterizable but stable for verification. The design shall also expose optional pulse or sticky flags for stale_reject and timeout_fault; if sticky, they shall clear only on reset or explicit clear input, which shall be synthesizable if included.

All arithmetic shall be fixed-point or integer and synthesizable. No floating-point operator is required unless explicitly added as a parameterized macro, which is not mandatory for this architecture. The design shall avoid combinational loops and shall register any long control paths as needed for ASIC timing closure. All interface handshakes shall be free of X-dependent logic and shall use explicit valid qualifiers. The implementation shall be RTL-clean, lint-clean, and suitable for an Arch2RTL flow targeting digital_ip_asic. The external DoMINO model interface shall remain outside the ASIC netlist and shall be referenced only through its input and output transaction contract.
